description: Single-Spark recipe for vcruz305's DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 SAGE EXL3 1.62 bpw pack (326.6 GB) with vLLM, from vcruz305/DSV4.1-Flash-1017-EXL3-Spark-recipe at 8036aa74; the Model is the revision the kit declares, c852150e (the later head 8cffca26 differs only in the README). It serves the creator's measured configuration: a 524,288-token window, one sequence, 2,112 batched tokens, a 1 GiB KV pool, prefix caching, DSpark with 5 greedy draft tokens and adaptive verification, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs for sizes 1 to 7, TileLang kernels, a disk Engram table, text only, the deepseek_v41 parsers, and the creator's defaults for requests that send none (32,768 output tokens, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95). Engine: the creator's base image is distributed only as a Hugging Face tar.zst the platform cannot pull, so the image is built from the kit's own source path: Christopher Owen's spark-ds41f r6w (2dc95329) prepared by its own code against its lock on the digest-pinned vllm/vllm-openai, justincasey's eight patches and overlays, then vcruz305's vllm-exl3 (30e8b941) and exllamav3 (909ad856), with a build-time sm_121 kernel scan of five files. Interface fix: the kit's Engram reader needs io_uring, which the sandbox blocks (the kit runs seccomp=unconfined). The image compiles it unchanged against a header-only liburing stand-in that does one pread() per read under the default seccomp profile, and the build check that the natives link liburing now asserts they link none. Engram reads may be slower than the creator's. Memory: the pack is far larger than the memory it runs in. Routed experts stay on NVMe and the GPU reads them from the page cache through read-only ATS mappings; the 1,418 coldest experts and the embedding are gathered into a 9,228,943,360-byte side file the launcher builds once into the persistent cache (CPU only, 9.2 GB of disk, checked against the shipped selection on every start). The two 101.5 GB Engram shards are read from disk and are not memory use. The creator measured a 110.5 GiB engine reservation, 3.1 to 3.2 GiB MemAvailable at ready and 2.19 GiB (the creator's shipped cold set); with under about 1.5 GiB of page cache at ready the cold experts are re-read every step and decoding runs about three times slower. The declared peak, 123.3 GB, is the 130,663,231,488-byte total less 2.19 GiB less the 5,012,574,208-byte idle use: an estimate until the hardware try, and the memory guard may refuse or stop it. The first boot compiles about 156 kernels; the recipe keeps the creator's serialised cold-cache settings (one worker, one TVM thread), which cost nothing measurable in his ready time and bought 1.24 GiB of headroom. Creator claims, not measured here: 27 to 35 tokens per second decode, 1,000 to 1,100 prefill, retrieval at 520K tokens. Licences are information only: weights and kit MIT, vllm-exl3 AGPL-3.0-only, spark-ds41f and the base patches Apache-2.0.
title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 SAGE EXL3 1.62bpw vLLM single Spark
